claims.claim: Coherence begins to fall apart within a few hundred words, and when asked for a style the model over-applies it.
claims.quote: It will often overdo the style you ask for
claims.page: How to make AI write a bestseller—and why you can't

claims.claim: AI tools flatten authorial voice, homogenise, and eradicate creative risk-taking by applying blanket rules without understanding purpose.
claims.source: Sophie Playle, fiction editor, Liminal Pages (2026-05-06)
claims.quote: They flatten voice and eradicate creative risk-taking.
claims.page: AI and Fiction Editing: Should You Use It, Can You Trust It and Will It Take Your Job?

claims.claim: The Granta AI story is lyrical nonsense with no narrative, reading like a parody of poet-turned-novelist fiction despite judges praising its 'lyrical precision'.
claims.quote: it does not have a story. There's no narrative.
claims.page: Lincoln Michel note on the Granta AI story

claims.claim: Tricolon and stacked triplets of descriptors are overused as a default rhetorical shape.
AI keeps repeating a shape or cliché where even a bad human writer would notice and rest it, because its instinct is to keep obeying the instruction.
claims.quote: Even bad human writers give it a rest when noticing repetition
claims.page: How to Identify AI-Written Web Fiction

claims.claim: Em-dashes are overused, roughly one per paragraph, and used for thought continuation rather than breaks.
claims.quote: AI does this on a sentence level often with those em-dashes
claims.page: What Makes a Story "Look" Like AI Wrote It?

claims.claim: AI holds an unnaturally locked point of view across scenes and paces every scene at the same rate.
claims.page: I Asked the Machine to Tell on Itself: A Field Guide to AI Tells

claims.claim: Generated casts sound like one person and generated scenes run too long on screen, breaking pacing (vendor source with a stake in the fix).
claims.quote: A whole cast that sounds like one person
claims.page: AI Dialogue Generator for Games: What Actually Works in 2026

claims.claim: MFA readers strongly disfavored prompted AI pastiches on stylistic fidelity (OR 0.16), but after fine-tuning on the author's corpus both MFA and general readers preferred the AI, and it was flagged as AI only 3% of the time; the tells above characterize prompted default-register output.
claims.quote: Fine-tuned outputs were rarely flagged as AI-generated (3% vs. 97%)
claims.page: Readers Prefer Outputs of AI Trained on Copyrighted Books over Expert Human Writers

claims.claim: 2,587 lay readers rated ChatGPT rewrites of three published short stories higher on quality and absorption than the originals and identified authorship at chance; the researchers attribute this to AI being clearer and more predictable, which is the same property editors name as the gloss.
claims.source: Sears and Weisberg (Villanova) via earth.com report (2026-08-04)
claims.page: Readers rated AI stories higher than human fiction in study of 2,587 adults

claims.claim: AI stories state their moral meaning directly instead of dramatizing it, favoring tidy single-track plots.
claims.quote: over-explain themes and favor tidy, single-track plots

claims.claim: Claude-generated stories in particular show flat event escalation compared with human fiction.
claims.quote: Claude produces notably flat event escalation

claims.claim: Human stories frame protagonist choices as morally ambiguous; AI stories resolve into clean internal acceptance.
claims.source: Russell et al., StoryScope; Dramatica gloss 2026-05-29

claims.claim: AI fiction runs one tight causal chain with far fewer subplots and more protagonist-driven resolutions than human fiction.
claims.quote: tighter causal chains, more protagonist-driven resolutions

claims.claim: Human stories use more time jumps, flashbacks and nonlinear delay of revelation; AI stories stay chronological.

verdicts.trueWording: The issue is that it will often overdo the style you ask for.
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim as a clause (source has lowercase 'it' mid-sentence). Coherence half also confirmed: 'Remember, coherence starts to fall apart at ~250 words.' and 'treat LLM output as suspect at 250 words; beyond 500, it'll be downright bad.'

verdicts.trueWording: They flatten voice and eradicate creative risk-taking.
verdicts.note: Exact sentence, punctuation included. Rest of claim also on page: 'They apply blanket rules, with no understanding of context or purpose.' and 'it flattens and homogenises.'

verdicts.trueWording: man, it does not have a story. There's no narrative.
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim. All three other elements confirmed: 'a particular brand of lyrical nonsense that is quite literally nonsensical', 'It does read like a parody of a certain type of poet-turned-novelist fiction', and 'Certainly extra embarrassing that "lyrical precision" was highlighted by the judges.' Note dated May 19, matching.

verdicts.trueWording: Products impress people; platforms empower them.
verdicts.note: Quote is ALTERED, not verbatim - 'people' and 'them' were dropped. Claim substance holds: entry reads 'Overuse of the rule-of-three pattern, often extended to four or five' and 'A single tricolon is elegant; three back-to-back tricolons (tri-tricolons) are a pattern recognition failure.' Source says stacked tricolons, not 'triplets of descriptors'.

verdicts.trueWording: even bad ones will 'give it a rest' when they notice
verdicts.note: Quote is a paraphrase, not verbatim. Full source sentence: 'A human writer might reuse words, but even bad ones will "give it a rest" when they notice.' The persistence half is verbatim-supported: 'Current AIs have the opposite instinct, to stick to instructions and generate text that seems to fit the previous paragraph.'

verdicts.trueWording: AI does this on a sentence level often with those em-dashes, declarative sentences.
verdicts.note: Quote appears word for word as the opening of that sentence, BUT in the emotional-resonance/deep-POV section, not the em-dash-overuse section - it is not the source's support for the claim. The claim itself is separately confirmed verbatim elsewhere: 'There's one in every paragraph.' and 'That's not a break in thought. It's a continuation of thought. That's an AI tell.'

verdicts.trueWording: Pacing flatness: scenes unfold at a constant rate.
verdicts.note: No quote was supplied, so verbatim is not assessable; both halves are on the page. POV half: 'POV lock: LLMs "pick a lane and stay in it with unnatural consistency" - no drift between free indirect style, interior monologue, and exterior scene', which Vollmer attributes to Charlie Guo rather than observing himself. Pacing line continues 'No elision, no selective summary.'

verdicts.trueWording: because one person wrote all of it at midnight
verdicts.note: MISATTRIBUTION. The quote is verbatim but describes HAND-WRITTEN dialogue, not generated dialogue: 'A whole cast that sounds like one person because one person wrote all of it at midnight.' It sits in the list of hand-authoring failures that 'AI dialogue generators promise to fix', immediately before 'AI dialogue generators promise to fix the speed problem.' The page's actual verdict on AI runs the other way: 'AI is excellent at volume and consistency and weak at the specific, surprising sentence.' Second half of the claim IS supported: 'Dialogue that looks fine in a document often runs too long on screen, breaks the pacing, or makes no sense next to what the player just did.'

verdicts.trueWording: Fine-tuned outputs were rarely flagged as AI-generated (3% vs. 97% for prompting) by leading detectors.
verdicts.note: Verified against raw arXiv abstract HTML, not just the fetch layer. Quote verbatim but truncated mid-parenthetical (drops 'for prompting'). OR=0.16 for MFA fidelity confirmed; 'Both groups preferred fine-tuned AI' confirmed. The trailing clause 'the tells above characterize prompted default-register output' is the analyst's own inference and is not in the paper.

Quote strips the hedge 'Perhaps', which carries the speculative force: 'Perhaps people generally prefer predictability, because difficult or subtle material requires more brain power.' Everything else confirmed: 2,587 adults, Sears and Deena Skolnick Weisberg at Villanova, three published stories rewritten by ChatGPT, higher quality and Story World Absorption Scale ratings, and the gloss link 'AI writing tends to be clearer, more direct and easier to process' plus 'the AI versions of our stories usually stated their themes explicitly'. One imprecision: 'at chance' is loose - experiment 2 was 39.93%, below chance ('worse than a coin flip'); only experiment 3 (51.97%) was at chance.

verdicts.trueWording: AI stories over-explain themes and favor tidy, single-track plots
verdicts.note: Verified against raw arXiv abstract HTML. Paper exists: arXiv:2604.03136, 'StoryScope: Investigating idiosyncrasies in AI fiction', Russell, Rajendhran, Pham, Iyyer, Wieting, submitted 2026/04/03.

verdicts.trueWording: Claude produces notably flat event escalation
verdicts.note: Verified against raw arXiv abstract HTML. In the abstract it is one of three per-model fingerprints, alongside 'GPT over-indexes on dream sequences, and Gemini defaults to external character description' - the 'in particular' framing is fair.

verdicts.trueWording: AI stories show tighter causal chains, more protagonist-driven resolutions, fewer subplots, and cleaner internal acceptance.
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim in the Dramatica article. Human-side half also present: 'more morally ambiguous protagonist choices' and 'Human stories are more likely to leave endings ambiguous, complicate responsibility, fracture time'. Article does cite Russell et al. StoryScope explicitly.

verdicts.trueWording: AI stories show tighter causal chains, more protagonist-driven resolutions, fewer subplots, and cleaner internal acceptance.
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim (same sentence as 147). Minor drift: the claim's intensifier 'far fewer subplots' is not in the source, which says only 'fewer subplots' with no magnitude. This is a secondary source glossing StoryScope, not the paper itself.

verdicts.trueWording: They use more temporal discontinuity, more flashbacks and nonlinear movement
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim. Delay-of-revelation half also present: 'more willing to let a revelation reshape earlier material rather than simply deliver the next clean cause in a line.' Drift: the source is strictly comparative (human stories use MORE); it never asserts the claim's absolute 'AI stories stay chronological.'
